claims.text: Preheating AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock and the build platform to approximately 600°C reduces thermal gradients during additive manufacturing.
The approximately 600°C preheat reduces residual stress relative to ambient-temperature, high-thermal-load processing.
The preheat promotes a more uniform microstructure.
The preheat improves mechanical properties relative to conventional ambient-temperature processing.
The as-received AlCrFeNiSi powder has a particle-size distribution typical of high-entropy-alloy feedstocks used in additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention applies controlled preheating to both the powder feedstock and build platform before and during fabrication.
The proposed processing setup uses a laser-based deposition system in an inert atmosphere.
The targeted miniature components have dimensions on the order of 5–10 mm.
A reduced solidification thermal gradient produces a more uniform grain structure.
A reduced solidification thermal gradient lowers the density of thermally induced defects.
Preheating lowers the density of dislocations characterized as thermally induced defects.
Preheating diminishes rapid cooling and quenching effects.
Diminishing rapid cooling and quenching mitigates residual-stress formation.
Mitigating rapid cooling and quenching preserves the mechanical integrity of fabricated components.
Preheated components are expected to exhibit greater tensile strength than ambient-processed controls.
Preheated components are expected to exhibit greater ductility than ambient-processed controls.
The hypothesis is bounded to miniature AlCrFeNiSi components fabricated in an inert atmosphere with a preheat window centered around 600°C.
Changes in preheat temperature, atmosphere, or component size may alter the outcome.
